newsitem.title: UK: Yorks Water plans sewage treatment upgrades.
newsitem.headline: Yorks Water plans sewage treatment upgrades.

text.p: British water and sewerage firm Yorkshire Water Plc said it would be spending around 120 million stg to improve coastal sewage treatment at four plants by 2000.
In a statement, Yorkshire said it also planned to speed up solutions for crude sewage outlets at some four small coastal villages.
A spokesman for the company said around 20 million stg of the planned investment was over and above levels already agreed under five year pricing arrangements.
The company said the moves were part of its new "COASTCARE" programme.
"The new and revised plans...go much further than any current legal requirements for coastal discharges," said chairman Kevin Bond.

Yorkshire said it would install preliminary, primary, secondary and ultra violet disinfection treatment at the plants at Scarborough, Whitby, Filey and Bridlington in north east England, where previously only primary treatment was planned.

Bond became chairman in April of 1996 after the company had been slammed for its handling of the 1995 drought, when it was on the verge of forcing customers to queue publicly for domestic water supplies at standpipes.

Yorkshire, which covers one of the wettest regions in England, was forced to tanker in water from neighbouging areas as the drought squeezed its pipeline infrastructure to the limit and showed up its shortcomings.
